To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 4q sub-telomere is remodeled in FSHD and the DUX4 transcription factor induces cell toxicity, which is the basis of the pathogenic mechanism of FSHD.
FSHD is caused by DUX4 gene expression from the 4q sub-telomere and that DUX4 induces a cascade of transcriptional changes that results in a loss of muscle mass.

(a) the 4q subterminal region contains a number of sequence variants which are associated with FSHD, (b) the FSHD-associated haplotypes contain a polyadenylation site immediately distal of D4Z4, (c) DUX4 is transcribed and translated in FSHD and (d) DUX4 induces cell toxicity in FSHD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
unravelling the molecular basis of FSHD and understanding its pathogenesis.
unravelling the molecular basis for FSHD and the development of novel therapeutic interventions for this condition.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in FSHD, with a view to developing new therapeutic strategies for this condition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FSHD is a DUX4-dependent myopathy.
FSHD is a D4Z4-dependent disorder in which a polyadenylation site in a specific 4q subtelemeric haplotype allows DUX4 to be expressed at levels sufficient to induce cell toxicity.
FSHD results from the ectopic activation of DUX4, which is a transcription factor with the capacity to induce cell toxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DUX4 gene is the FSHD-causing gene and the DUX4 mRNA and protein are the pathogenic products.
FSHD is caused by the inappropriate expression of DUX4 in muscle.
FSHD is a disease of the telomere and that the disease phenotype results from the inappropriate expression of the DUX4 gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular basis of FSHD can be attributed to the activation of a single gene, DUX4, which is normally repressed in somatic cells.
FSHD is caused by a single transcriptional event that is dependent on the 4q sub-telomere sequence.
the D4Z4 repeat array at 10qter is not a major contributor to FSHD pathogenesis, and the DUX4 protein is the key pathogenic agent in the disease.
